on_screen_text: Robert Quigg (1885-1955) was awarded the Victoria Cross medal for most conspicuous bravery at the Battle of the Somme.

"On 1 July 1916, he advanced to the assault with his platoon three times. Early next morning, bearing a runner that his platoon officer was lying out wounded, he went out seven times to look for him under heavy shell and machine gun fire, twice returning back a wounded man. The last man he dugged in on a waterproof sheet from within a few yards of the enemy's wire. He was seven hours engaged in this most gallant work, and finally was exhausted that he had to give it up."
After his service with the army, he returned home to live near Bradmills and is buried in the graveyard of Billy Parish Church.
